key_insight: Universal Textual Teaching (UTT) distills teacher-student knowledge gaps into a reusable natural-language artifact called a Primer, avoiding parameter updates while improving LLM reasoning and code performance.
engineering_relevance: This makes knowledge distillation more portable and practical for API-only, expensive, or architecture-mismatched models because the learned guidance can be reused across checkpoints and even students.
method: Identify representative teacher-student failure cases via paired evaluation.
Use a multi-role loop: Student attempts, Prompter converts feedback into instructions, Teacher supplies targeted demonstrations, Synthesizer merges validated lessons.
Iteratively refine a textual Primer that captures the distilled teaching signal in reusable natural language.
evidence_signal: Across Omni-MATH-2 and KernelBench, the abstract reports large gains, including math accuracy from 27.6% to 51.7% and KernelBench Student accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% (Fast1 from 9% to 35%).
watch_item: Because the Primer is synthesized from observed gaps, its quality may depend on representative evaluation cases and careful prompt orchestration to avoid overfitting to a specific teacher-student pair.
